data.reasoning: The deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash report provides a complete and sound analysis: the PKGBUILD fetches from the package's own declared upstream GitHub repository (aunetx/blur-my-shell) at a fixed tag (v73) with a checksum, uses standard build tooling (make), and performs no network operations or code execution beyond normal packaging. No malicious injection, no execution of fetched content, no fetching from unrelated hosts. The other reports were inconclusive due to tool failures (API errors, parsing errors), not analytical disagreement.
data.disagreement_analysis: The 'disagreement' was triggered by inconclusive results, but there is no actual analytical disagreement. Report 1 (qwen) failed on 4/5 files due to HTTP 400 API errors. Report 3 (openrouter, advisory-only) had a parser failure on PKGBUILD despite the model providing a valid safe analysis. Only Report 2 (deepseek) completed successfully with a safe verdict, and its reasoning is correct under the threat model.

learnings: Distinguish tool failures from analytical disagreements when triggering re-audits - API errors and parser failures should not count as 'disagreement'
Implement retry logic or fallback models when API calls fail with HTTP 400 errors
Improve parser robustness to handle varied model response formats, especially when the model provides valid analysis in non-standard XML structure
Advisory-only reports should be clearly separated from voting reports to avoid confusion in disagreement detection
